Subject: Trial plan & model shortlist for multilingual product search POC

Hi Lucie / Paul —

Great to meet today — thanks for the 30 minutes and walkthrough of the current search flow. Quick post-call recap and a concrete POC proposal so we can get things moving: 

Summary of ask
- Goal: prove a production-feasible model that improves product search relevance across EN/ES/FR for Acme’s web + mobile storefronts; maintain latency targets for interactive search (low sub-200ms net added).
- Scope: ranking/relevance + query rewriting/normalization for multi-lingual queries; not intent classification or personalization in this first phase.

Proposed success criteria (we should confirm numbers):
- Relevance: +8–12% gain in precision@10 (benchmarked against current Lucene-based ranker) on the supplied query sample set.
- Latency: 95th percentile inference <= 250ms for single-query online calls (p50 ~<120ms).
- Stability: <2% of responses with hallucinations / factual drift for sample product metadata.
- Cost guideline: incremental inference cost <= $0.50 per 1k queries at expected volume during trial.

Model shortlist and recommendation (open models):
1) Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (server-side quantized) — balanced for instruction-style ranking and multilingual tokenization; good English + Spanish baseline.
2) Secondary/fallback: Llama-2-13B-Weight-Quant (8-bit) — stronger for long context ranking if we need higher accuracy and can tolerate higher cost/latency.
3) Safety/fallback lightweight: OpenAssistant-v2 (7B) for quick failover in degraded capacity scenarios.

Notes about multilingual: we recommend tokenizing queries with SentencePiece and include locale-specific normalization rules for ES/FR. We'll validate measured F1 per language slice during the eval.

POC plan (4 weeks) — high level
Week 0 (this week): kickoff, data handoff, confirm evaluation queries and KPIs.
Week 1: infra setup — hosted trial instance on Redwood (or Dedicated if you prefer), model provisioning and baseline inference numbers.
Week 2: evaluation run — run A/B across model variants on held-out query set; produce per-language breakdowns.
Week 3: tuning and final report — hyperparameters, batching/quantization tradeoffs, cost/latency analysis, recommended production rollout plan.

Ownership
- Acme: Lucie (product lead), Paul (engineering lead) — provide evaluation query set, sample product metadata export, and a test account.
- Redwood: Jordan (sales owner), Diego (SE lead for infra & eval harness), Evelyn (CS — success criteria / rollout).

Open questions / asks from our side
- Can you share a 2–3k query sample across EN/ES/FR (anonymized) + a small product metadata extract (product id, title, category, short description)?
- Do you have any strict PII/data-routing constraints (VPC/on-prem vs hosted)?
- Procurement timeline / PO window (Paul I think there was a mid-Oct procurement slot?)

Attachments: I attached a simple POC evaluation template and a one-pager model brief for quick sharing with engineering.

Next steps
- If you confirm the dataset + procurement window, we can schedule infra kickoff for Mon 10/5. Diego and I will hold capacity.
- Proposed 30-min kickoff: Mon 10/5 09:30 PT.

Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Hi Lucie / Jordan — putting a few technical notes here so expectations are clear.

1) Tokenization & accents (ES/FR)- Mistral-Instruct-7B has decent multilingual tokenization for short queries, but accent normalization is largely solved at the preprocessing layer (we recommend NFKC normalization + accent-stripping as an explicit rule for titles, then re-run model scoring). If you prefer language-specific handling we can add a small locale-aware rewrite step before model inference.

2) Latency estimates (single-query online calls)- Mistral-7B quantized (int8) on a modern A10/A30 class GPU: p50 ~60–90ms, p95 ~180–240ms depending on batching.- Llama-2-13B quantized (int8) on same infra: p50 ~120–180ms, p95 ~260–340ms. Observable delta depends on batching and KV cache utilization.

3) Throughput & cost at ~150 qps- With continuous batching and small prefixes we can sustain 150 qps with 2-3 GPUs for the Mistral setup; Llama-13B will require additional capacity (3–4 GPUs) and will therefore increase instance cost ~1.6–2x. We'll provide an estimated cost sheet in the kickoff.

4) Eval harness and metrics- We'll run A/B on your held-out queries and produce per-language precision@10, nDCG, hallucination flags (simple product-matching heuristics), and latency distribution. I recommend adding a quality gate: if p95 latency > 300ms for any model slice, we don't promote it to production in this POC.

5) Hosted VPC options- We can support VPC peering for the trial (Redwood Dedicated or hosted with VPC peering); it requires a quick network config call but is standard. For a one-month test it's feasible — procurement will want a short SOW to reflect the network work.

Happy to join the kickoff and walk through infra.
